# ACORD form filler: how to fill ACORD 125, 126 and 140 automatically


Abhi Balijepalli


Co-founder, CopyCat


Published November 16, 2026


·


9 min read


The short version


- A commercial submission is mostly the same facts typed into several ACORD forms: the insured, the operations, the locations, the vehicles, the drivers and the losses. An ACORD form filler types them once.
- Agencies fill ACORDs four ways: by hand in a fillable PDF, printed from the agency management system, through a digital application the client completes, or with AI that reads the account’s documents.
- AI filling is only worth it if every value is cited to its page, gaps are flagged instead of guessed, and you can edit any field on the form before it goes out.
- CopyCat[ACORD Submissions](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-form-automation) fills every ACORD form from prior ACORDs, dec pages, loss runs, MVRs and schedules, and CopyCat is a member of ACORD.


Ask an account manager where the week goes and ACORD forms come up fast. The client sends last year's application, three dec pages, a loss run, an MVR for every driver and a vehicle list in a spreadsheet. Someone then retypes the insured's name, address, FEIN, class codes, vehicles, drivers and five years of losses into the ACORD 125, again into the 126, again into the 127, 129 and 163, and again into the 140. Every retyped value is a chance for a typo that an underwriter will notice before you do.


This guide covers what an ACORD form filler does, the four ways agencies fill ACORDs today and where each one breaks, how AI ACORD automation works, and what to check before you send a filled form to a market. We make CopyCat, so read our recommendation with that in mind.


## What goes into a commercial submission


A typical commercial submission is an ACORD 125 plus one section per line of business. The same facts repeat across them, which is why filling them by hand is so slow.


Form What it covers Where the answers usually live


[ACORD 125](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-forms/acord-125) Commercial insurance application: agency, applicant, lines of business, locations, nature of business, prior carriers, loss history Last year’s application, dec pages, loss runs


[ACORD 126](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-forms/acord-126) Commercial general liability section: hazards, class codes, exposures, schedule of hazards GL dec page and class schedule


[ACORD 127](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-forms/acord-127) ,[129](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-forms/acord-129) ,[163](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-forms/acord-163) Business auto section, vehicle schedule and driver schedule Auto dec page, vehicle spreadsheet, MVRs


[ACORD 130](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-forms/acord-130) Workers compensation application: rating by state and class, payroll, officers WC dec page, payroll by class


[ACORD 131](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-forms/acord-131) Umbrella and excess section, with the underlying policies Umbrella dec page and the underlying decs

## The four ways agencies fill ACORD forms


Method How it works Where it breaks


By hand An account manager types into each fillable PDF. Slow, and every form is typed separately, so the same value can differ from form to form.


From the management system The AMS prints ACORDs from the client record. Only as good as the record. Losses, vehicles, drivers and dec page details still have to be keyed in first.


Digital applications The client answers an online questionnaire that maps to ACORD fields. Depends on the client finishing it. Renewals already have the answers in last year’s documents.


AI from documents Software reads the account’s documents and fills every picked form at once. Only as trustworthy as its sources. Without citations and gap flags you are back to checking every box.


Most agencies mix these. The management system handles the certificate and the simple renewal, and the hard commercial submission, the one with eight vehicles, two locations and a loss history, goes back to someone typing. ## How AI ACORD automation works


ACORD names every field on its forms with a stable data label, and the same label appears on every form that asks for that fact. The applicant's name is the same field on the 125, the 126 and the 140. That makes one data model per account possible: read the facts once, then fill every form that asks for them.


An AI ACORD filler worth using does four things:


- **Reads every document you have.** Prior ACORDs and carrier apps, dec pages, quotes, loss runs, MVRs, SOVs, schedules in Excel and intake notes, scanned or not.
- **Cites every value.** Each fact points back to its page, such as "Loss runs, p. 3", so checking a value takes one click.
- **Carries over what it can, and only that.** Last year's ACORD can prefill a box, but it never proves this year's coverage.
- **Flags what is missing.** If no document gives the year built or the FEIN, the box is marked for review. A filler that guesses to make a form look complete is worse than a blank.


## Checklist: before you trust an AI-filled ACORD


- Are the forms the current ACORD editions? The ACORD 125 and 126 moved to 2025/03 and the ACORD 130 to 2026/08.
- Does every value show the document and page it came from?
- Are unanswered questions flagged for review instead of filled with a guess?
- Can you edit any field directly on the form, and tick or clear a checkbox?
- When you change one fact, does it update on every form that carries it?
- Do you get a finished PDF for each form that any carrier will accept?
- Does anything leave the agency without a person reviewing it? It should not.
- Does the vendor train models on your clients' documents? Ask for the answer in writing.


ACORD forms are copyrighted and used under license. Ask any vendor where its forms come from and which editions it fills. CopyCat is a member of ACORD.


## Filling a submission with CopyCat, step by step


1. **Drop the documents.** Last year's ACORDs and carrier apps, dec pages, loss runs, MVRs, the vehicle spreadsheet and the SOV, in any order. Add the client's website if you want it read too.
2. **Pick the lines.** General liability brings the 125 and 126, commercial auto brings the 127, 129 and 163, property brings the 140. CopyCat suggests forms the documents point to, and you add or remove any ACORD.
3. **Review the cited facts.** The build lists what it read, the named insured, operations, revenue, vehicles, drivers, losses and locations, each with its page.
4. **Check the forms in the editor.** Open any ACORD, click a field to change it, and clear the boxes marked for review. Or tell the assistant "FEIN is 84-2291736, and add umbrella" and it updates the 125 and adds the 131.
5. **Download and send.** Download each PDF, or Download all for one zip with every form and a marketing summary workbook. Email summary drafts the submission email to the markets in your list that write these lines, for you to send.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is an ACORD form filler?


Software that completes ACORD insurance forms, such as the ACORD 125, 126 and 140, so nobody retypes the same account details into every form. The newest fillers read the account's documents and fill the forms from them, citing each value to its page.


### Can AI fill ACORD forms automatically?


Yes. It is trustworthy when each value is cited, gaps are flagged instead of guessed, and you can edit any field before the submission goes out.


### Which ACORD forms are used in a commercial submission?


The ACORD 125, plus a section per line: 126 for general liability, 127 with the 129 and 163 for auto, 130 for workers compensation, 131 for umbrella, 140 for property and 160 for a businessowners policy.


### Can my agency management system fill ACORD forms?


Most can print ACORDs from the client record. Anything that only lives in documents, such as losses, vehicles, drivers and dec page detail, still has to be keyed in first. An AI filler reads those documents directly.
